<!-- pr-reviewer: f8a8ff8d67254702254a7aef1b548da7ef020a3d -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

Independent review of head `f8a8ff8d`, trial-merged with `origin/main` at `2bc79a3c` (clean merge, no conflicts). Judged against #1168's "Done means": a release build ignores the variable, pinned by a test, and the agreement lane keeps its own way to pick the field engine. All three hold.

### What looks good
- **Only one place reads the variable.** I searched the whole tree for `CAMCRAFT_CARRY_ENGINE` and `CARRY_ENGINE_ENV` (all `.rs`, `.toml`, scripts, workflows and docs). The only read is `default_engine()` in `crates/app/src/stock_sim_held.rs:79-87`. The other hits are docs, the re-export, and the existing test guard at `carried_engine_agreement.rs:272`, which reads the variable but never sets it. MCP, the CLI, the UI and posting all get their engine from `stock_sim::carry_engine()`.
- **The release profile really turns the switch off.** The workspace `Cargo.toml` sets only `[profile.dev]` (`debug = "line-tables-only"`) and `[profile.dev.package."*"]` (`opt-level = 1`, `debug = false`). There is no `[profile.release]` and no per-crate profile, so the release build keeps Cargo's default `debug-assertions = false`. `release.yml` (`cargo build --locked --release ...`) and `cargo xtask release` (`xtask/src/release_pack.rs:86`, `build --release`) both use that profile, and neither sets `RUSTFLAGS` or `-C debug-assertions`. So `CARRY_ENGINE_SWITCH_HONOURED` is `false` in what ships, and `default_engine()` returns `Column` without reading the environment.
- **Default builds and goldens are unchanged.** The default is still the column engine. On that engine `engine_note()` returns `None`, so `sim_clause`, `simulate_verdict` and the Deviate status text are byte-identical to main, and no golden file is touched.
- **Every user-facing verdict names the field engine.** It appears in the post gate's visible line (`posting_sim.rs:57`, which reaches the post result, status line and G-code header through `verification_report_by`), the setup sheet `SIM:` line (`setup_sheet/mod.rs:152-159`) and the GUI Deviate readout (`crates/ui/src/actions.rs:118-120`). The text is plain English and follows the existing `note:` pattern from #1094's void note.
- **The tests do not depend on the process environment.** The new tests never set an environment variable. They use the pure `engine_from_switch(value, honoured)` and the thread-scoped `with_carry_engine`, so they are safe in parallel runs.
- No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` outside tests. The decision note is filed per PR. The `Changelog:` line, the `Fixes #1168` line and the conventional subject are all present. No snapshot PNGs, goldens, dependencies, `build.rs`, `.github/` or process files are touched.

### Local results (merged with main, Windows, debug)
| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --lib` | 147 passed |
| `carried_engine_agreement` | 3 passed, 1 ignored (heavy lane, untouched) |
| `stock_sim_document` | 9 passed |
| `carried_verify` | 8 passed |
| `setup_sheet` | 7 passed |
| `post_not_judged` | 4 passed |
| `posting` | 17 passed |
| `setup_carry` | 9 passed |
| `rest_across_setups` | 7 passed |
| `carried_fixtures_cache` | 6 passed |
| `CAMCRAFT_CARRY_ENGINE=field` (debug, switch honoured): `carried_engine_agreement` / `setup_carry` / `carried_verify` / `rest_across_setups` | 3 (+1 ignored) / 9 / 8 / 7 passed. The slower run times (26 s, 47 s, 13 s) show the field arm is really selected. |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib` (CWD `crates/ui`) | 615 passed, 5 ignored |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

### Requested before merge
None.

### Notes (not blocking)
1. **An unknown value is ignored without a log line.** In a debug build, a typo such as `CAMCRAFT_CARRY_ENGINE=feild` falls back to the column engine (`stock_sim_held.rs:73-76`) and nothing is logged. This was already the case before this PR, it only affects dev builds, and the fallback is the shipped engine. A `log::warn!` in `default_engine()` for a set value other than `field`/`column` would make it visible. This could be a P7 follow-up.
2. **MCP `render_stock` does not carry the note.** Its summary (`crates/app/src/mcp/render.rs:74-92`) runs `simulate_document` but adds no engine note. A shipped build is not affected (always the column engine). It matters only for a dev build with the switch set, and `mcp_verify`/post results already carry the note through `sim_clause`.
3. **The note goes into the "not judged" field.** It rides `SimClause::not_judged` (as #1094's void note already does), so a clean field-engine verdict now has `not_judged = Some("note: ...")`. Any code that reads `not_judged.is_some()` as "the sim did not judge" will see a note there, but only on the field arm, never in a release build. Worth keeping in mind when #589 flips the default and `engine_note` inverts.
4. **The note is per thread.** `engine_note()` reads the calling thread's engine. That is correct here, because the sim and the note are read on the same thread. A future caller that runs the sim on a job thread and builds the note elsewhere would need to pass the backend along.
5. **File size.** `crates/ui/src/actions.rs` is 407 lines after the merge (main has 404), already past the ~400 guide. This is a flag, not a blocker.
6. **Not exercised:** a real `--release` build with the variable set. The release behaviour rests on the `cfg!(debug_assertions)` constant and the absence of a release-profile override (confirmed above). Also not run: the heavy `--ignored` agreement lane, the GUI readout by hand, macOS and Linux.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
